sentences.text: How do the Dutch choose who runs their country?
At least every four years, you get one vote.
With a red pencil, you fill in the box next to one candidate.
Each party gets seats in line with its votes.
Together, they fill the 150 seats of the House of Representatives.
It makes laws, approves the budget, checks the government and can even vote it out.
Then the 75 senators check every law, but they can only say yes or no.
Provincial councils choose them, not you directly.
No party wins 76 seats alone. In 2025, D66 and the PVV tied with just 26 each.
So three parties teamed up, with Rob Jetten as Prime Minister.
And the head of state? Nobody votes for him.
He signs every law, but his ministers carry the responsibility.
Is it really democracy if you don't vote for your head of state?
